earlier_scan.source_named: Weitlaner, Roberto J. 1948. Un Idioma Desconocido del Norte de Mexico (sole description of Naolan; short wordlist article)
earlier_scan.note: Only extant description is a phonetically transcribed wordlist; stress coverage doubtful (Wikipedia transcriptions show no stress marks)

sources.citation: Zamponi, Raoul. 2024. Extinct lineages and unclassified languages of Mexico. In Søren Wichmann (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of Mexico and Northern Central America, 99-158. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Modern re-analysis of Weitlaner's Naolan data with a phonological inventory (cited by es.wikipedia for consonants and syntax); most likely modern source to interpret the accent marks and say whether stress/tone is recoverable.

sources.citation: Stresser-Péan, Guy. 2000. Capítulo 12. Los pisones de la Sierra Madre Oriental. In San Antonio Nogalar, 597-610. Mexico: CEMCA (OpenEdition Books, freemium).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Ethnohistory: Weitlaner obtained 'de indígenas muy ancianos, un vocabulario de 44 palabras' at San Juan de Naolán west of Tula; summarizes the Uto-Aztecan (Weitlaner) and Tonkawa (Swadesh) classification proposals. Site is behind an Anubis challenge by automated download, so no file.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 1979. Middle American languages. In Lyle Campbell & Marianne Mithun (eds.), The Languages of Native America: Historical and Comparative Assessment, 902-1000. Austin: University of Texas Press. §1.14.1 Naolan, pp. 948-949.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Classification only: 'It was all but extinct when Weitlaner (1948b) collected the only known material, 43 words and phrases, in 1947.. For now the language should be considered unclassified' (pp. 948-949); reference entry '1948b Un idioma desconocido del Norte de México. ICA 28.205-27.'

sources.citation: Swadesh, Mauricio. 1968. Las lenguas indígenas del noreste de México. Anales de Antropología 5(1).
sources.note: Comparative re-examination of the Naolan wordlist (Tonkawa hypothesis); may re-transcribe the forms and comment on the accent marking. UNAM OJS is behind an automated-access block by automated download; DOI resolves 404.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en). Naolan language (reproduces Weitlaner 1948 wordlist and phrases; cites Weitlaner 1948 and Campbell 1997).
sources.note: No statement on stress. The transcriptions do carry acute accent marks on some forms (masúːná, má sá mò'ːná, ma sóna, ma namuléa, manáme, má'ː-yo, ma kuyóam, sána, móːlan, ma sóče, ma paján, tatačú, míː, nóːkil, nyó'ːke, jotuní wáːna, čupájo, kosúsameːuwampa ƀiːtóːya) and length marks — this refutes the earlier scan note that 'Wikipedia transcriptions show no stress marks'. Accent position varies (initial, penult, final) across the few forms; no rule can be read off.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (es). Idioma naolano (wordlist; 'Descripción lingüística: Fonología' section; cites Weitlaner 1948, Zamponi 2024, Swadesh 1968, Stresser-Péan 2000).
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent placement. Claims vowel length is contrastive (marked with macron below) and 'Además, parece poseer un sistema tonal' citing Weitlaner — unverifiable editor inference, not quoted from a source; the same forms carry acute accents (mí̱, sána, ma sóna, ma náme, mó̱lan, ma kuyóam, jotuní wá̱na, chupájo, paján, má̱yo).

sources.citation: Wiktionary. Appendix: Naolan word list (same Weitlaner 1948 reproduction).
sources.note: Nothing; wordlist only, same accent marks as en.wikipedia.
Nothing; records that the only descriptive source is Weitlaner 1948 (Glottolog's most extensive description type a wordlist or less, 23 pp., in Spanish); no coordinates, no other refs.
